titulo_es: To say where you are and what languages you speak

texto: To ask where you're from, you say «Waar kom je vandaan?». See that «vandaan» goes to the end. To answer: «Ik kom uit...» (I come from / I am from...). To ask for languages: «Spreek je Nederlands?» (Do you speak Dutch?). With the pronoun «je» postponed to the verb in questions, the verb loses the -t final: «spreek je» (and not «spreekt je»).

frases.nl: Een beetje. Ik spreek Spaans en Engels.
frases.es: Un poco. Hablo español e inglés.
frases.en: A little. I speak Spanish and English.

bloques.pregunta: How is the «where» question said in Dutch?

opciones.explicacion: It's the question pronoun of place.
It means «from where» (origin / source).
It is the «de» or «from» preposition.
«Ik kom uit» indicates source («I come from Spain»).
It indicates future direction, not origin.
He speaks of language, not of the country of origin.

bloques.pregunta: Complete with the origin preposition («I come from»).

opciones.explicacion: «uit» is used to indicate the country or city of origin.
It is combined with «waar» at the beginning: «Waar kom je vandaan?».
It is the copulative conjunction «and».

bloques.pregunta: What is Noor asking in this sentence?

opciones.explicacion: She asked if you spoke the Dutch language.

opciones.texto: Do you live in the Netherlands?
opciones.explicacion: I would ask for residence («Woon je...»).
I'd ask for hearing understanding.

bloques.explicacion: Remember to put «vandaan» at the end of the question.

bloques.pregunta: What verbal form corresponds to the second person «jij komt»?

opciones.explicacion: This is the form of present for «jij» in direct affirmative order.
It is the form of first person («ik kom»).
It is the verb to speak («ik spreek»).
conjugated form of the verb komen («jij komt»).
It corresponds to «spreekt».
It corresponds to «woont».

opciones.texto: A little. I speak Spanish and English.
opciones.explicacion: «Een beetje» means a little; «Spaans en Engels», Spanish and English.
